metaDescription: Border Terrier vaccine schedule with core ages in weeks. Set reminders so Border Terrier boosters are not missed.

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: The Border Terrier core series (DA2PP / DHPP plus rabies per law) is plotted at 8, 12, 16, 16 weeks in the table above so a small puppy is covered as maternal antibodies fade.
At 11-15 lb (5-7 kg), Border Terrier visit logistics matter as much as antigens: book the 16-week appointment before class, daycare, or boarding asks for proof.
Bring canine epileptoid cramping syndrome risk and hip dysplasia into the Border Terrier exam-room conversation while you are already there for shots.
Rabies for a Border Terrier still follows local statute, and when the clinic allows you can pair it with the ≥16-week core finish, then photograph the certificate into PetClues the same day.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Owners postpone Border Terrier shots when the puppy seems “a little off,” travel intervenes, or canine epileptoid cramping syndrome risk worries dominate the week — ask the clinic whether a same-week Border Terrier make-up is still appropriate instead of sliding to the annual exam.
Long gaps can leave Border Terrier antibody levels uncertain, so expect either an added booster or a titer conversation rather than a shrug.
Do not trade the missed Border Terrier dose for extra socialization; finish immunity first for this small dog.
Reset the Border Terrier reminder stack the evening of the make-up appointment — including the eventual adult booster after the 16-week finish.

faqs.question: When does the Border Terrier core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Border Terrier misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read Border Terrier health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the Border Terrier adult health guide for breed predispositions such as canine epileptoid cramping syndrome risk, then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
